standard.title: Grammatical morphemes and word families
standard.description: recognise and know how to use grammatical morphemes to create word families
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words (AC9E1LY14). At Foundation level students understand that words can be made of more than one meaningful part (AC9EFLY15). They have not yet systematically used grammatical morphemes — inflectional endings such as -s, -ed, -ing, -er — to generate and recognise word families.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and use grammatical morphemes to create and read word families.

nodes.label: Morphemes carry meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that words can be made of more than one part (base word + morpheme) and that each part contributes meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the base word and added morpheme in at least two examples (e.g. 'walk-ed', 'play-ing') and explain what each part contributes.
nodes.typical_width: Identify base words and grammatical morphemes in familiar words, explain how the morpheme changes the meaning or grammatical role of the base, using examples like 'play', 'plays', 'playing', 'played'.
wider: Explore how the same base word changes function with different morphemes — noun to verb, verb to adjective
Discuss how recognising a base word inside a longer word helps with reading and meaning

response_modes.reason: Identifying base word and morpheme requires a segmenting reasoning move — 'what is the core word, what was added?' A simple scaffold ('find the word inside the word') supports students in making this move reliably.

success_criteria: Student identifies the base word in a morphologically complex word
Student names the morpheme added and explains what it changes

nodes.label: Common grammatical morphemes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and use common grammatical morphemes — -s, -es, -ed, -ing, -er — to create word family members.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least three different grammatical morphemes to build new word forms from a given base word.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and use common grammatical morphemes to create word families — plural -s/-es, past tense -ed, present continuous -ing, comparative -er — from familiar base words.
wider: Build extended word families from common morphemes and discuss what each form is used for
Explore morphological families that include compound forms (e.g. 'playground', 'playtime' from 'play')
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who do not have a working set of common grammatical morphemes cannot apply morpheme knowledge as a reading and spelling strategy in N3 — the N3 integration task requires knowing what the morphemes are before using them as decoding and encoding tools.

response_modes.reason: Students often recognise -ing and -ed but miss plural and comparative morphemes. Encountering all common grammatical morphemes as a coherent family — not individual spelling rules — builds the broader morphological awareness needed.

success_criteria: Student correctly builds at least three word family members from a base word using different morphemes
Student reads a morphologically complex word by identifying the base word first

nodes.label: Using morphemes to read and spell
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use morpheme knowledge to read unfamiliar words by recognising base words, and to spell by applying morpheme addition.
nodes.minimum_width: Read an unfamiliar word by identifying the base word inside it; spell at least two words formed by adding a morpheme to a known base.
nodes.typical_width: Apply morpheme knowledge to read unfamiliar words — recognising the base word and then the morpheme — and to spell words formed by adding known morphemes to known base words.
wider: Discuss what happens to some base words when morphemes are added — e.g. 'hop' → 'hopped' (doubling) — at awareness level only
Use morpheme knowledge to self-correct reading errors — identify whether the base word was read correctly

response_modes.reason: Using morphemes as a reading and spelling tool integrates knowledge of base words and morpheme function into an active decoding and encoding strategy — the endpoint of this strand's progression at Year 1.

success_criteria: Student reads a morphologically complex word by identifying the base word
Student correctly spells a word formed by adding a familiar morpheme to a known base
